title: A morphism of affine schemes is formally unramified iff its ring map is formally unramified
statement: Let $f:Z\to X$ be a morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme], $R=\mathcal O_X(X)$, $S=\mathcal O_Z(Z)$, and $\varphi=f^\sharp:R\to S$ the induced ring map, so that $f$ is identified with $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $f$ is formally unramified [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism] if and only if $\varphi$ is a formally unramified ring map: for every $R$-algebra $A$, every ideal $I\subseteq A$ with $I^2=0$ and every $R$-algebra map $a:S\to A/I$ there is at most one $R$-algebra map $a':S\to A$ lifting $a$.
